packages.name: Add-ScriptSignature
packages.title: Add-ScriptSignature
packages.description:
This script will sign a script with a self signed certificate.
If a certificate is not found, the script will return a warning and prompt the user to create a self signed
certificate.
The script will also check if the file is already signed and return a warning if it is.
The script will also add a timestamp to the signature to ensure the signature is valid for a longer period of time.
The script uses the timestamp server: <http://timestamp.digicert.com>.

packages.name: AdvancedVPNDeployment

packages.description:
Big Thanks to Paul Stancer and Jeff Winn for their skills and efforts in making this module possible.
Paul Stancer's 'VPNCredentialsHelper' module is a dependency for this module to work. This module will automatically install Paul's module upon using the creation function of this module if it is not installed prior.



Creates advanced VPN Connection. This is built with Meraki VPN connections in mind but should be able to create any VPN connection other than EAP current as that requires additional input for certificates.

This tool has only been currently tested for Meraki L2TP connections.




Please send any feedback, reviews, comments, concerns and/or questions to powershellcoder@outlook.com

Im interested in knowing any feedback and also suggestions.




Use:

[ Create-AdvancedVPNConnection -Syntax ]
[ Connect-VPNConnection -Syntax ]


for syntax, examples and notes on the use of this module.




Included Functions:


Create-AdvancedVPNConnection

Connect-VPNConnection

Disconnect-VPNConnection

packages.name: AutopilotDeviceSync
packages.title: AutopilotDeviceSync
packages.description:
This script checks all the Autopilot-related devices to make sure that they are named correctly, have the right attributes (e.g. Group Tag
and Purchase Order ID), and aren't redundant (e.g. because the device has been deployed multiple times, creating a new Hybrid AADJ device
each time).  By default, this script will just display information about what isn't in sync.  If you want it to actually fix it, you have
to specify additional command line paraemters.  At present, extra Hybrid Azure AD devices can be removed from Active Directory (with 
-CleanDevices switch) and device name issues can be fixed (with -FixNames).

Due to the amount of data this will retrieve, it is possible this won't work for large tenants due to Graph API throttling.

packages.name: SimplySql
packages.title: SimplySql
packages.description:
Querying SQL (SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSql, SQLite, & mySql) the PowerShell way: simple commands... powerful opportunities.

SimplySql is a module that provides an intuitive set of cmdlets for talking to databases that abstracts the vendor specifics, allowing you to focus on getting work done.  The basic pattern is to connect to a database, execute one or more sql statements and then close your database connection.  This module provides cmdlets that map to this basic pattern.  Each provider has its own Open-*Connection cmdlet -> Open-SqlConnection, Open-SQLiteConnection, Open-OracleConnection, Open-PostGreConnection, Open-MySqlConnection.  The rest of the commands are provider agnostic.

Open/Close/Show/Test/Set/Get -SqlConnection >> Control as many active connections as you want.
Invoke- SqlScalar/SqlQuery/SqlUpdate >> Interact with those connections.
Get/Clear -SqlMessage >> Get Informational messages, if provider supports it.
Invoke-SqlBulkCopy >> Bulk Dataload from one connection to another.
Start/Complete/Undo -SqlTransaction >> Utilize transactions!
